data.name: Hunt
data.gender_notes: Hunt is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English word 'hunta', meaning 'pursuer' or 'hunter'. This name has been popular in English-speaking countries for centuries, and was often given to children born into families with a strong hunting tradition. The name Hunt carries the meaning “Pursuer, Hunter” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hunt usually hope their child will grow to embody pursuer, hunter and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.name: Χαντ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Χαντ προέρχεται από την αγγλική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'κυνήγι' ή 'αναζήτηση'. Στην ελληνική γλώσσα, το όνομα συνδέεται με την ιδέα της αναζήτησης πνευματικής σημασίας ή σύνδεσης με τον Θεό. Το όνομα δεν αναφέρεται άμεσα στη Νέα Διαθήκη, αλλά η ιδέα της αναζήτησης του Θεού είναι κεντρική στο Χριστιανισμό.

in_latin.name: Hunt
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Hunt ex lingua Anglica originem habet et significat 'venari' vel 'spiritualem significationem quaerere'. In Ecclesia Christiana, nomen Hunt ad notionem venationis spiritualis refertur, quae est investigatio mysteriorum Dei et vitae spiritualis.

Historically, the name Hunt has been used in various Christian cultures, signifying a person of strong faith and devotion.
